question: A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus" -> "resistant to acyclovir" -> "acyclovir is ineffective" -> "famciclovir is an alternative" -> "famciclovir is effective against VZV" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus" -> "requires alternative antiviral treatment" -> "ganciclovir is primarily for CMV" -> "ganciclovir not effective for VZV" -> "cidofovir is a broad-spectrum antiviral" -> "cidofovir has limited use for VZV" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus" -> "not responsive to acyclovir" -> "famciclovir has better bioavailability" -> "famciclovir is effective for shingles" -> "recommended for elderly patients" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus" -> "requires effective antiviral treatment" -> "cidofovir has activity against VZV" -> "but has significant side effects" -> "not first-line for shingles" -> 65%

CHAIN: "Thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus" -> "increased risk of complications in elderly" -> "need for effective antiviral therapy" -> "famciclovir is a suitable option" -> "improves outcomes in shingles" -> 88%
analysis: Thymidine kinase-deficient strains of varicella-zoster virus (VZV) are resistant to acyclovir, which relies on this enzyme for activation. Famciclovir is also less effective against such strains. Ganciclovir is primarily used for cytomegalovirus infections and is not the first choice for VZV. Cidofovir is an alternative antiviral that can be effective against VZV, especially in resistant cases. Amantadine is not effective against VZV. Therefore, cidofovir would be the best choice for treating shingles caused by a thymidine kinase-deficient VZV strain.
